symptom: On Mendix 9.x and 10.0–10.20 every workflow was refused: `this Mendix 9.24.30 project cannot store Workflows$Workflow.PersistentId (Mendix 10.21.0+)` (25-rename on 9.24)
cause: The workflow writer (and the ALTER WORKFLOW mutator, for the activities it inserts) mints a fresh PersistentId on the workflow and on every activity, outcome and boundary event. PersistentId is 10.21.0 on all four (Workflow, and the abstract WorkflowActivity, Outcome, BoundaryEvent). The floor refused the workflow's own and never saw the rest, because it does not look up abstract supertypes
file: `modelsdk/canon/versionshape.go` (LowerToProjectShape: dropPersistentID on every Workflows$ element below 10.21)
insight: **An identity the writer mints is not a value the statement said**, so below its version it is dropped, not refused (unlike ForceFullObjects, which a script can set). Lower it in canon.LowerToProjectShape rather than encodeWorkflow: wfmutator's raw inserts (mutator.go: PersistentId on inserted activities, outcomes, boundary events) never pass encodeWorkflow, but every write passes normalizePropertySetsFor. **Test with a non-zero GUID**: a zero GUID is an empty value the floor silently drops, so the first draft of the test passed on the unfixed code. **The floor-off build + `mx convert -p` 9.24 key diff** showed the whole picture at once: PersistentId on 6 element types, plus the empty keys the floor already handles. The same run found the next gap: a `parallel split` writes Workflows$EndOfParallelSplitPathActivity (a 10.21 type) and 9.24 does not load the project (TypeCacheUnknownTypeException) — not fixed here. Measured: bug-test on a fresh 9.24.30 app → exec ok, mx check 0 errors, mx convert strips no key (adds WorkflowOnStateChangeEvent/UsertaskOnStateChangeEvent null). 25-rename 9.24 FAIL→PASS; 25-rename and 24b on 10.24.24 and 11.13 PASS. Tests: TestNormalize_WorkflowPersistentIDsBelowMendix10_21; mdl-examples/bug-tests/1163-workflow-on-mendix9.mdl
